sections.title: Growth and identification
sections.text: Common vetch is a scrambling annual that may climb or trail to about 2 m. Its pinnate leaves usually have 3–8 pairs of leaflets and a branched terminal tendril. Pea-like flowers, singly or in groups of up to three, range from white and pink to blue-purple; the cylindrical pods may reach 7 cm and hold up to 12 seeds. The image's purple flowers, tendrils and pod fit this species.

sections.title: Forage and seed safety
sections.text: It is widely cultivated for forage, but its seeds are not a straightforward pulse: some lines contain beta-cyanoalanine-related compounds and other antinutritional factors. Cultivation as livestock forage does not imply that raw seed is safe for people; species, cultivar and processing matter.
